study type: Secondary analysis of a multicenter prospective study
cohort: 6,489 women attempting trial of labor after cesarean delivery (TOLAC) who reached +2 station with a fully dilated cervix
finding: In laboring women with a previous uterine scar, attempting OVD is associated with greater maternal morbidity and less neonatal morbidity than LRCD.
mod_finding: Attempting operative vaginal delivery (OVD) was associated with greater maternal morbidity, largely driven by perineal injury, compared to laboring repeat cesarean delivery (LRCD).
